duration_overflow.text: overflow when adding duration to instant

findings.question: Open edge of the RE-005 TLS value-object packet (PR #2935: body 0x5ce30d0 listed as beyond its boundary) and of the RE-005 park_timeout provenance packet (PR #2938: "the contention fallback body 0x5ce30d0 that registration_b calls when its byte claim fails"), answered against the same authenticated artifact: what is the body, which paths reach it and under what conditions, what does it produce, and can it actually fire?
findings.identity: SETTLED. The body 0x5ce30d0..0x5ce3426 is the park core of the vendored tokio multi-thread scheduler: its three assertion panics carry Locations in .../z_vendor/tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/park.rs (lines 179, 211, 213, recovered from .rela.dyn RELATIVE addends). It operates on the per-thread park cell Q -- in registration_b, the field at [r13+0x10] of the handle object taken from the caller's argument -- using the state word at [Q+8], the guard byte at [Q+0x18] and the wait key at [Q+0x10]. It never reads or writes [Q+0], the shared-inner pointer whose byte claim gates entry.
findings.sole_route: SETTLED. The whole-.text rel32 census finds exactly one reference to the body in the artifact: call 0x5cec9ec inside registration_b 0x5cec8b0. No tail jump targets it, no 8-byte stored pointer in the file equals its start, and no .rela.dyn RELATIVE addend names it, so no indirect route (function table, vtable, callback) reaches it either.
findings.entry_conditions: SETTLED. Both entries share the tail at 0x5cec9e7, which hardwires esi = 0 and edx = r15d (the nanos word) with rdi = Q unchanged since 0x5cec934. Sentinel arm: nanos == 0x3b9aca00 (cmp pin 0x5cec938), the state-word consume CAS 3 -> 0 at 0x5cec948 failed, and the byte claim on the shared inner at [S+0x50] (S = [Q+0]) at 0x5cec95e failed; the sentinel is reloaded into r15d at 0x5cec964 on this arm, so the call passes (0, sentinel). Finite arm: nanos != sentinel, the byte claim at 0x5cec9c8 failed, and nanos != 0 -- the test at 0x5cec9e2 with the je at 0x5cec9e5 skips the call for a zero nanos. In both arms the byte is held by a sibling registration_b execution on the same shared inner, and the holder keeps it across its entire selector park (claims at 0x5cec95e / 0x5cec9c8; release by the xchg at 0x5ceca09 after the selector call returns), so contention lasts for a whole park, not a spin window.
findings.supply: SETTLED. registration_b is called only from top_reg_b 0x5cecc60, whose three call sites supply edx in {0, sentinel} only: xor-zeroed at 0x5cece57 and 0x5ced565, the sentinel constant loaded at 0x5ced788 (the provenance packet records the same census). A zero nanos takes the finite arm of registration_b, whose fallback call is gated off, so in this artifact the fallback is entered only with (secs = 0, nanos = sentinel) and only its indefinite-park arm can execute. Its finite-duration arm -- deadline = clock 0x5c842e0 now plus the pair, with the std checked-add overflow panic (std/src/time.rs line 429), the remaining recomputed through instant_sub 0x5c84210 at 0x5ce3213, and the timed wait at 0x5ce3286 -- is structurally present but no caller in the pinned graph supplies it a finite nonzero duration.
findings.inside: SETTLED, for the reachable arm. The body first claims the cell's own guard byte [Q+0x18] (0 -> 1 CAS at 0x5ce30ee); if the byte is already set it waits through GOT slot 0x64e01f8 (byte_wait 0x5bb59d0) with (byte pointer, 0x3b9aca00) and continues to the state word regardless. It then CASes the state word [Q+8] 0 -> 1 (0x5ce3100): an old value of 3 is a raced notification, consumed by the xchg to 0 at 0x5ce3312 with an immediate return; an old value other than 0 or 3 panics "inconsistent park state; actual = {}" (park.rs line 179, Location static 0x64c5a20). Otherwise it waits in the loop at 0x5ce31b5: the wait helper is loaded from GOT slot 0x64e73b8 (wait_helper 0x5bb4670) and called with (Q+0x10, Q+0x18, sentinel) until the state CAS 3 -> 0 at 0x5ce31d3 succeeds. The exit at 0x5ce3316 releases the guard byte (1 -> 0 CAS at 0x5ce331a); if that CAS fails, the exit tail-calls the notify helper through GOT slot 0x64e0f38 (byte_notify 0x5bb5650) with (byte pointer, 0). The wait/notify call shapes (pointer + timeout / pointer + 0) are the same guard idiom the RE-001 queue-table packets pinned. The body is the only writer of state value 1 in this graph.
findings.difference: SETTLED. The claim-success arms park through the shared inner: the state word is driven 0 -> 2 (wrapper_state at 0x5cec9d9 on the finite arm, registration_b's own CAS at 0x5cec973 on the sentinel arm) and the thread sleeps in the io/time selectors. The fallback touches no shared state: the loser parks its own thread on its own cell through the scheduler wait table, cycling the state word 0 -> 1 -> 0 instead of 0 -> 2 -> 0, and neither claims nor releases the holder's byte. registration_b discards the fallback's return value (the jump at 0x5cec9f1 goes straight to the shared continuation at 0x5ceca0d) and stores the same pre-claim flag -- bpl is 1 on both fallback arms -- into the returned object at +0x74 (pin 0x5cecac1), so the only observable trace of the fallback in the returned object is the intermediate state value.
findings.panic_surface: SETTLED. Four panics are encoded in the body: park.rs line 179 "inconsistent park state; actual = {}", line 211 "inconsistent park_timeout state, actual = {}", line 213 "invalid park_timeout state, actual = {}", and the std "overflow when adding duration to instant" (std/src/time.rs line 429). On the reachable arm only the line 179 check sits on the path, and the pinned writer graph produces only 0, or a raced 3, for this cell at that point: firing it needs a state the graph's writers do not produce, i.e. it is the source-level consistency assertion. The line 211/213 panics guard the finite arm's exit switch (jump table at 0x94cb10: old state 0 -> line 211 panic block 0x5ce32ca, 1 -> exit 0x5ce3316, 2 -> line 211 panic block, 3 -> exit; an old state above 3 goes to the line 213 panic at 0x5ce339d) and are unreachable from the pinned caller graph, as is the overflow panic.

open_edges: Who writes state value 3 to a cell (the notify/unpark side), and through which entry points a wake targets a specific cell, is not traced here; the fallback only consumes 3.

The internals of the wait helper 0x5bb4670 and of the guard wait/notify helpers 0x5bb59d0 / 0x5bb5650 are RE-001 territory; this packet pins only their GOT slots, extents, digests and the call shapes the fallback uses.

Whether any body outside the exported/pinned set also claims the byte at [S+0x50] on the shared inner is not censused here; within the caller graph above registration_b the only claim and release sites are registration_b's own.
Open edges 1, 2 and 4 of the TLS value-object packet, and the forwarder time-context writers edge of the provenance packet, remain open.
